label: Pitts et al., 2017
citation: Pitts NB, Zero DT, Marsh PD, Ekstrand K, Weintraub JA, Ramos-Gomez F, et al. Dental caries. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17030.
verified_scope: PubMed record and abstract: caries as a biofilm-mediated, sugar-driven, multifactorial dynamic disease.

label: Moynihan and Kelly, 2014
citation: Moynihan PJ, Kelly SA. Effect on caries of restricting sugars intake: systematic review to inform WHO guidelines. J Dent Res. 2014;93(1):8–18.
verified_scope: Europe PMC MEDLINE core record and abstract, PMID 24323509: evidence relating sugars intake and caries across the life course; no inference about this survey’s dietary measurements.

label: Margozzini et al., 2020
citation: Margozzini P, Berrios R, García-Huidobro R, Véliz C, del Valle C, Vargas JP, et al. Number of remaining teeth and its association with educational level in Chilean adults: data from the National Health Survey 2016–2017. Int J Dent. 2020;2020:8848190.
verified_scope: Primary article and author-institution bibliography: ENS oral-examination procedures, complex survey design and education/tooth-loss association. Does not identify the examination weight variable; its n=5,473 is not this analysis cohort.

label: Uribe et al., 2026
citation: Uribe SE, Carrasco-Labra A, Schwendicke F, Maldupa I. Prognostic clinical predictive models for dental caries using artificial intelligence: methodological considerations. Caries Res. 2026 Jul 16. doi:10.1159/000553309. Online ahead of print.
verified_scope: Karger online-first listing and Europe PMC MEDLINE core record/abstract, PMID 42461868: validation, calibration and clinical usefulness in caries prognostic modelling; cited as a methodological review, not journal policy or evidence that this cross-sectional model predicts incidence.

label: Fisher et al., 2019
citation: Fisher A, Rudin C, Dominici F. All models are wrong, but many are useful: learning a variable’s importance by studying an entire class of prediction models simultaneously. J Mach Learn Res. 2019;20(177):1–81.
verified_scope: Primary JMLR publication page and abstract: dependence of importance on model choice and importance variation across well-performing models. This study does not estimate model class reliance. No DOI is listed by JMLR.

label: Strobl et al., 2008
citation: Strobl C, Boulesteix AL, Kneib T, Augustin T, Zeileis A. Conditional variable importance for random forests. BMC Bioinformatics. 2008;9:307.
verified_scope: Europe PMC MEDLINE core record and abstract, PMID 18620558: correlated predictors can affect unconditional permutation importance. This study uses marginal, not conditional, permutations.

label: Collins et al., 2024
citation: Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, Riley RD, Beam AL, Van Calster B, et al. TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods. BMJ. 2024;385:e078378.
verified_scope: PubMed/PMC record and statement abstract: reporting guidance for regression and machine-learning prediction studies. Citing the checklist does not certify compliance.

label: von Elm et al., 2007
citation: von Elm E, Altman DG, Egger M, Pocock SJ, Gøtzsche PC, Vandenbroucke JP; STROBE Initiative. The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement: guidelines for reporting observational studies. Lancet. 2007;370(9596):1453–1457.
verified_scope: PubMed record/abstract and EQUATOR guidance: reporting of observational studies, including cross-sectional designs.

label: Breiman, 2001
citation: Breiman L. Random forests. Mach Learn. 2001;45(1):5–32.
verified_scope: Primary Springer publication record and author’s Berkeley random-forests page: original algorithm reference.

label: Varma and Simon, 2006
citation: Varma S, Simon R. Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection. BMC Bioinformatics. 2006;7:91.
verified_scope: PubMed/PMC record and abstract: bias when cross-validation model-selection scores are reused for error estimation; rationale for nested validation.

label: Roberts et al., 2017
citation: Roberts DR, Bahn V, Ciuti S, Boyce MS, Elith J, Guillera-Arroita G, et al. Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography. 2017;40(8):913–929.
verified_scope: Primary Wiley article: validation that respects dependence structures. Supports grouping related observations, not a claim of external validation or official ENS survey weighting.

label: Steyerberg et al., 2010
citation: Steyerberg EW, Vickers AJ, Cook NR, Gerds T, Gönen M, Obuchowski N, et al. Assessing the performance of prediction models: a framework for traditional and novel measures. Epidemiology. 2010;21(1):128–138.
verified_scope: PubMed record/abstract and author-institution record: discrimination, calibration and overall prediction error assess distinct aspects of performance.

label: Christodoulou et al., 2019
citation: Christodoulou E, Ma J, Collins GS, Steyerberg EW, Verbakel JY, Van Calster B. A systematic review shows no performance benefit of machine learning over logistic regression for clinical prediction models. J Clin Epidemiol. 2019;110:12–22.
verified_scope: Crossref publisher metadata and Europe PMC MEDLINE core record/abstract: review found no evidence of superior ML performance over LR and identified validation/reporting limitations; not a claim that all algorithms are equivalent in every dataset.
